New concept used: varicella_containing_vaccine = any varicella-containing dose (VAR or MMRV), because the text says 'VAR or MMRV may be administered' and mixed series (e.g. VAR then MMRV) must count together; the vocabulary has separate varicella_vaccine and mmrv_vaccine concepts only.

Routine schedule timing (dose 1 at 12–15 months, dose 2 at 4–6 years) is not encoded as separate age-specific rules (e.g. dose 1 expected by age 2, two doses by age 7) because that would require derived ages; completion is checked only through the age 7–18 rule.
Minimum age (12 months) for a valid dose is not checked; doses given before 12 months would be counted.

Minimum intervals are not checked: dose 2 as early as 3 months after dose 1 (age 12 and under; a dose after at least 4 weeks may be counted as valid) and 4–8 weeks routine / 4 weeks minimum interval for age 13 and older.

Product choice not represented: for dose 1 at age 12–47 months MMR and varicella vaccines are recommended to be given separately, with MMRV allowed by parent/caregiver preference; maximum age for MMRV is 12 years.

Evidence of immunity (per MMWR rr5604) is not computable from structured data; the denominator therefore includes an uncomputable criterion and the rule will report 'not computable' unless immunity status is supplied.
Contraindications/precautions are not listed in this section and are not represented as exclusions.
